subtopic: A power cut or rain spoils plans
passage: The colony picnic at the park had been rained off, so the families gathered in the community hall instead. Harsha's father, Omkar, spread a mat, his mother unpacked sandwiches, and a board game came out of a bag. Harsha dragged a chair to the wall and folded his arms. "Everything is spoiled," he said. His little sister held up the dice. "No." Around the mat, the games got louder and someone started a song. Harsha watched from his chair, chewing a cold sandwich, hearing every laugh. When it was time to go home, he realised he had spent the whole cosy afternoon looking at it from across the room.

qa.q: Where did the families gather after the picnic was rained off?
qa.a: The families gathered in the community hall.

qa.q: What was Harsha feeling as he sat by the wall, and how does his behaviour show it?
qa.a: Angry and disappointed, since he folded his arms, said everything was spoiled and refused the game.

qa.q: What could Harsha have done instead of sulking, and why?
qa.a: He could have joined the board game and treated it as a different kind of picnic, because the day was still there to enjoy.

qa.q: How might Harsha's father feel seeing him sit apart?
qa.a: Probably sad and a little helpless, since Omkar had spread the mat to make the day cosy and Harsha would not join.

grounding: A boy whose picnic is rained off sulks and blames, and misses the cosy day the family arranged.
